claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Unfortunately, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**Age threshold exceeded**: The most significant factor is that Alex is 21 years old. According to UK government guidance, Child Benefit can continue for children aged 16 or over only if they are **under 20** and stay in approved education or training. Since Alex is 21, they are beyond the maximum age limit for Child Benefit eligibility.

Additionally, even if Alex were under 20, there are two other disqualifying factors:

1. **Working 24+ hours per week without being in approved education**: The rules state that you'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training.

2. **Receiving qualifying benefits in their own right**: You'll also stop getting Child Benefit if your child starts getting certain benefits such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit in their own right.

Since Alex meets all three disqualifying criteria (but most importantly, exceeds the age threshold), you cannot claim Child Benefit for them.

reasonings: According to the official UK government guidance, Child Benefit eligibility for a child aged 16 or over has specific requirements. Alex is 21 years old, which means they fall under the extended eligibility rules that apply to 16-20 year olds. The guidance states: 'You'll normally still qualify for Child Benefit if your child is under 20 and they stay in approved education or training.' However, it also specifies: 'You'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child: starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training, starts an apprenticeship in England, or starts getting certain benefits, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit.' Alex's circumstances show that: 1) Alex is 21 years old (over the 20-year age limit for extended Child Benefit), 2) Alex works 24+ hours per week and is not in approved education, and 3) Alex receives qualifying benefits (UC, ESA) in their own right. Any one of these factors would disqualify eligibility, but all three apply. Most critically, Alex exceeds the maximum age threshold of 20 for children in education or training. Therefore, you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.
